name: Voriconazole
executiveSummary: Broad-spectrum azole (aspergillus). Adult IV: load **6 mg/kg every 12 h × 2**, then **4 mg/kg every 12 h**; PO ≥ 40 kg **400 mg every 12 h × 2**, then **200 mg every 12 h**. Monitor levels and hepatotoxicity.
indications:
## Indications

- Invasive aspergillosis (treatment of choice in many protocols).
- Esophageal/invasive candidiasis due to fluconazole-resistant species; selected *Scedosporium* / *Fusarium* infections.

## Precautions

- Hepatotoxicity, visual hallucinations, photosensitivity, QT, strong CYP interactions.
- IV with cyclodextrin: caution in renal failure (CrCl < 50) — prefer PO.
- Orientative trough levels ~1–5 µg/mL by center.

> Take PO 1 h before or after meals.

adulto.dose: IV: load **6 mg/kg every 12 h × 2 doses**, maintenance **4 mg/kg every 12 h**. PO ≥ 40 kg: load **400 mg every 12 h × 2**, then **200 mg every 12 h** (< 40 kg: load **200 mg every 12 h × 2**, then **100 mg every 12 h**). May escalate to 300 mg PO every 12 h if response is insufficient.
adulto.administration: IV: reconstitute and dilute to 0.5–5 mg/mL; infuse **1–3 h** (max 3 mg/kg/h). No bolus. PO relatively fasting.

pediatrico.dose: Ages 2–12 (IV): load **9 mg/kg every 12 h × 2**, maintenance **8 mg/kg every 12 h** (max **350 mg every 12 h**). PO 2–12 years: often **9 mg/kg every 12 h** (max 350 mg). ≥ 12 years / ≥ 50 kg: adult scheme. Adjust by levels.

neonatal.dose: ID only; not a standard neonatal candida sepsis regimen (prefer ampho/echinocandin/fluconazole by focus).

stability:
## Stability

- Diluted IV: per label; do not refrigerate reconstituted solution on many brands.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Transient visual changes, hallucinations, rash, photosensitivity, ↑ transaminases, nausea, QT prolongation, neuropathy with prolonged use.
